LESSON: READING 11.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: FICTION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.2: Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: why reading fiction materials is important. 1. Which story books or plays have you read?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. distinguish between fiction and non-fiction reading materials
2. select and read grade appropriate fiction materials
3. keep a portfolio of the subject matter

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. distinguish between fiction and non-fiction reading materials
   In simple words: practise until you can distinguish between fiction and non-fiction reading materials. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. select and read grade appropriate fiction materials
   In simple words: practise until you can select and read grade appropriate fiction materials. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

3. keep a portfolio of the subject matter
   In simple words: practise until you can keep a portfolio of the subject matter. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction.
4. Show that you can: distinguish between fiction and non-fiction reading materials

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction important for a Grade 9 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read self-selected fiction materials and use a graphic organizer to write short summaries of the subject,
2. In groups, make a readers’ gallery by displaying the material read with a caption indicating its subject matter,
3. Take photos of their display and keep a soft and hard copy of the photo in their portfolio,
4. Write a card with the title and the subject matter of the material read and keep it in their portfolio,
5. Critical thinking and problem solving: It is cultivated as the learner researches from different sources the difference between fiction and non-fiction materials.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. why reading fiction materials is important. 1. Which story books or plays have you read?
2. What makes a book interesting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. distinguish between fiction and non-fiction reading materials
2. select and read grade appropriate fiction materials
3. keep a portfolio of the subject matter

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
